ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Egyptian domestic terrorism list (Law No. 80 of 2002, Article 21, and EMLCU circulars). Mandatory PEP identification for family members and close associates under FATF Recommendation 12 with enhanced due diligence for any detected PEP. Screening results are recorded in the UBO file and retained a minimum of five (5) years under the AML Law, Article 28.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, www.gafi.gov.eg) and the Egyptian Commercial Registry electronic portal of the Ministry of Trade and Industry (Tijara e-services) for name clearance requests.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered company name must be in Arabic; a Latin-script transliteration or foreign-language version may be added but never replaces the Arabic name. Foreign names are transliterated phonetically into Arabic according to passport spelling, and the legal suffix must read 'LLC' in English or 'شركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة' in Arabic. The chosen name must not be confusingly similar to an existing registered mark or trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant must file a written grievance with the Commercial Registry Grievance Committee under the Ministry of Trade and Industry within fifteen (15) days of the rejection notice, requesting re-examination with corrected tokens or transliteration. If the grievance is denied, the applicant may lodge a judicial appeal before the Economic Court within thirty (30) days of the adverse administrative decision. Alternatively, the applicant may resubmit a modified name, which resets the clearance cycle.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as the sole registered seat for an industrial manufacturing entity. The Commercial Registry and the Industrial Licensing Authority require a physical premise evidenced by a notarized lease of at least one (1) year and Civil Defense zoning approval. A virtual office may serve only as a supplementary correspondence address and cannot support the industrial operating license or VAT registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65 percent - an unannounced physical on-site inspection is probable within the first twelve (12) months from issuance of the industrial operating license, conducted by the Industrial Development Authority, the governorate, or Civil Defense. EMLCU AML on-site inspection for this low-risk equipment B2B trade is estimated at 15 percent.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association and Incorporation Certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum paid-up capital of 100,000 Egyptian Pounds, deposited in a licensed Egyptian bank escrow account and verified prior to registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of the Egyptian Limited Liability Company resolves unanimously to: (1) subscribe to the initial share capital of 500,000 Egyptian Pounds; (2) adopt the registered office at 123 Nile Street, Cairo, Egypt; (3) appoint Mr. Ahmed Hassan as Chairman and Managing Director, Ms. Fatima Ali as Financial Manager, and Mr. Karim Mahmoud as Company Secretary; (4) authorize the immediate filing of the Articles of Association with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and the Ministry of Trade and Industry for registration; and (5) commence business operations only after obtaining all required industrial, environmental, and civil defense clearances. This resolution shall remain effective until revoked by a subsequent Board resolution.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Adherence to Egyptian Environmental Law No. 4/1994 and its amendments, with specific limits on air emissions (e.g., particulate matter < 50 mg/m³), wastewater discharge (pH 6-9, BOD < 100 mg/L), and hazardous waste management per EEAA guidelines

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and safety inspection certificate from the Civil Defense Authority, building structural certification, and occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Manpower

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), a semiautonomous body within the Egyptian Ministry of Finance; official e-service portals include https://www.eta.gov.eg (unified tax registration, filings, and TIN issuance) and https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg (electronic invoicing and e-receipt clearance engine).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must obtain a unified statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) through the ETA's electronic registration module. The LLC's authorized Egyptian resident manager (or legal representative holding a notarized, legalized power of attorney) files the following bundle: (i) updated Commercial Registry extract showing incorporation of the LLC; (ii) notarized and legalized articles of association (MoA/AoA) and board resolution appointing the representative; (iii) proof of registered office/lease address in Egypt; (iv) passports of shareholders and managers; and (v) a certified bank statement showing the subscribed share capital account (no statutory minimum capital applies to the LLC). The ETA verifies the file, issues the unified TIN and activates the LLC as an established taxpayer for CIT, VAT, withholding, payroll, and stamp taxes; VAT registration under the same TIN is automatic once the annual taxable turnover exceeds the EGP 500,000 threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The Egyptian LLC is a juridical resident entity fully subject to entity-level corporate income tax under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005, as amended. It is taxed on worldwide profits (a territorial/production rule also captures Egypt-sourced income), at the tiered CIT schedule of 19% on the first EGP 10 million of annual taxable income and 22.5% above that band. Egypt does not recognize pass-through taxation for LLCs; distributions are not deductible and profit-bearing distributions are within the statutory dividend rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt has no U.S.-style check-the-box election. Available statutory mechanisms are: (i) the Investment Law No. 72/2017 regime election between the Inland Tax-Incentive Zone, the Free-Zone regime, or the Special Economic Zone regime for projects approved within the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone); (ii) the option to register voluntarily for VAT below the mandatory EGP 500,000 threshold in order to preserve input-VAT credit and export-refund rights; and (iii) treaty-relief elections applying to non-resident counterparties through the ETA's advance double-tax-treaty reduction procedure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended, together with Executive Regulations No. 66 of 2017 and ETA e-invoicing protocols.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supply turnover for mandatory VAT registration; voluntary registration is available below the threshold, and the same unified TIN is used as the VAT ID.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered businesses must transmit all invoices (B2B) and receipts (B2C) in the ETA-mandated structured XML/JSON format, in real time, to the ETA clearance API (https://api.invoicing.eta.gov.eg). The ETA performs immediate schema validation, digital-signature verification, and value/Rule-ID checks, returning a unique invoice UUID and a digitally signed QR stamp (two-dimensional fiscal seal) that must appear on the issued document. Unstamped/unaccepted invoices are legally non-compliant and input VAT may not be deducted. ERP-integrated filing, certified fiscal clearance portals, and e-receipt generation are compulsory phases already applicable to manufacturing exporters; no analogue fiscal-journal hardware stamping is applied.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of tangible goods from Egypt to a destination outside Egypt qualifies for the 0% VAT rate under Law 67/2016 where the exported equipment physically leaves Egyptian customs territory, the EG LLC is the exporter of record on the customs export declaration, the zero-rated invoice is issued and cleared through the ETA e-invoicing platform, and the export price is received and repatriated in convertible foreign currency through an Egyptian licensed bank within the statutory 180-day FX deadline. Export-related technical services (offshore installation, commissioning, and training) may also be zero-rated only if the place-of-supply rules assign the services to the foreign customer with performance occurring outside Egypt; services physically performed inside Egypt remain standard-rated or exempt as provided.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA electronic declaration) duly stamped and released by the Egyptian Customs Authority
Bill of Lading (or Airway Bill / international waybill) naming the EG LLC as shipper and a foreign consignee
Zero-rated commercial invoice transmitted and QR-stamped in the ETA e-invoicing system
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed Egyptian bank evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Packing list and non-preferential/preferential certificate of origin accompanying the shipment
Signed foreign sales contract and purchase order evidencing the commercial counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are cross-checked by the ETA against ASYCUDA customs release data, the e-invoice repository, and the banking FX-inflow records maintained by the Central Bank of Egypt. If the exporter fails the export-evidence chain, the proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, or the true value is understated, the ETA retroactively re-characterizes the supply as domestic at the standard 14% VAT rate, assesses the tax together with a monthly delay penalty (2% per month of the assessed VAT), and may impose VAT-evasion fines up to EGP 500,000 and imprisonment. Additional consequences include denial of input-VAT refund, customs wrongful-export penalties, and automatic blocking of the company's e-invoicing account and export licenses until the assessed liabilities are settled.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) is the sole foreign-exchange supervisory authority in the Arab Republic of Egypt, exercising its mandate under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020 and the Foreign Exchange Regulations issued by the CBE Board of Directors. The CBE licenses authorized banks, supervises the interbank foreign-exchange market, maintains the external position and capital-movement registry, and jointly operates the Advanced Cargo Information (ACI / Nafeza) platform with the Customs Authority for import-payment verification. The General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) administers the inward foreign-investment registration file that conditions future capital and profit repatriation rights.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt is in a market-clearing, flexibly managed exchange-rate regime since the full float measures enacted in 2024. Current-account transactions are broadly convertible for bona fide commercial flows: imports of machinery, spare parts, royalties, and service fees are settled against genuine contracts, pro-forma invoices, and the ACI customs order without case-by-case central-bank pre-approval. Capital-account entries are administratively registered rather than prohibited: foreign-direct-investment capital for the LLC must enter through an authorized bank, be credited to a capital entry account, and be recorded with the CBE and GAFI to establish the basis for future remittances. Profit repatriation for a foreign shareholder is lawful under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and is gated by (i) the tax clearance certificate confirming settlement of the 22.5% corporate income tax under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and applicable dividend withholding tax, (ii) the LLC's audited financial statements, and (iii) bank records evidencing the original inward remittance. Practical hurdles are liquidity-driven: during interbank scarcity windows banks may queue USD transfers, so the LLC should secure a committed USD repatriation facility and a rolling, documented dividend policy from the outset.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds for goods shipped from Egypt must be repatriated into the exporter's account at an authorized Egyptian bank within 90 days from the bill-of-lading / on-board date under the CBE Foreign Exchange Regulations implementing Law No. 194 of 2020 and the ACI/Nafeza framework. A documented extension up to 180 days is available for capital-goods transactions — relevant to ISIC 2819 integrated laser cutting systems — where the underlying sales contract lawfully provides a deferred payment schedule and the bank accepts the commercial contract as evidence. The exporter may credit the proceeds to an Egypt-domiciled foreign-currency retention account or convert them into EGP at the interbank market rate; no statutory flat surrender percentage applies in the current flexible-rate policy, although the CBE may issue temporary directives imposing a minimum conversion ratio during FX-stress episodes. Non-compliance, such as proceeds parked offshore or settlement outside the statutory window, triggers bank compliance alerts, exclusion from new import/export trade financing, and civil sanctions. The LLC must therefore execute export sales under irrevocable letters of credit or documented telegraphic-transfer terms with collection milestones inside the repatriation window.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — offshore digital EMI accounts (Wise Business, Payoneer, Airwallex, MultiPass and similar) are not acceptable as principal corporate treasury or export-collection accounts. The CBE repatriation rules require export proceeds to be collected into an authorized Egyptian bank within the statutory window; routing receivables to a foreign EMI would constitute a repatriation breach, render the receipts invisible to the CBE/GAFI registration records required for future profit remittances, and create tax and audit mismatches in the Egyptian books. A narrow ancillary use is permissible for collecting low-value deposits from regional distributors via locally licensed fintechs under the Payments Law No. 18 of 2019, subject to immediate onward transfer to the tier-1 bank account and full SWIFT reconciliation. The blueprint mandates a single primary tier-1 bank relationship, with domestic fintech payroll solutions used only for local salary and petty-cash flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for corporate account opening in Egypt. Under the CBE AML/CFT Instructions issued under the Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended) and Law No. 194 of 2020, the LLC's directors, each authorized signatory, and every natural-person ultimate beneficial owner with 25% or greater equity must attend a face-to-face interview at a bank branch; identity documents are visually verified, specimen signatures are executed before the compliance officer, and the Customer Due Diligence / Enhanced Due Diligence forms are signed on site. Remote video onboarding is not available for corporate clients. Where the shareholder is a foreign parent, the parent's notarized and legalized board resolutions, powers of attorney, and group organizational chart must be produced. The bank additionally conducts a physical site visit to the factory address declared in the commercial register, verifying the industrial license or lease supporting the ISIC 2819 manufacturing scope. The total lead time is generally 7 to 15 business days, including GAFI register alignments and correspondent-bank approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital introduced by a foreign shareholder domiciled in, or funds routed through, a high-risk or FATF-monitored jurisdiction without audited history of the parent company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete bankable file comprising the parent company's certificate of incorporation and commercial-register extract; consolidated audited financial statements under IFRS for the latest three years; notarized board resolution approving the Egyptian investment; UBO declaration reaching the natural-person level with passport, source-of-funds documentation, and tax returns; CBE-format KYC questionnaire; and a transaction-pattern schedule aligning the equity entry with the LLC's signed OEM and import contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared low-risk manufacturing activity (fiber laser cutting systems) and rapid amendments of the commercial-register scope, or formation through a third-party agent without active industrial premises.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full GAFI one-stop-shop incorporation folder containing the memorandum and articles of association, capital-deposit certificate, and subscription statements; industrial license or lease for the factory; invoices and customs entries for the first machine builds; site-visit photographs; insurance policies; and supplier and customer master lists with ACI/Nafeza registration numbers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large outbound USD payments, such as letters of credit for Chinese fiber-laser components, requested immediately after account opening and disproportionate to subscribed capital and unaudited sales pipeline.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Binding purchase contracts and purchase orders from the machinery supplier; draft LC terms and inspection certificates; the ACI customs-order registration record; a 12-month treasury plan with cash-flow milestones; letters of intent from downstream steel-fabricator clients; and VAT and advance-tax filings evidencing genuine purchasing and trading activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or senior director is a Politically Exposed Person, holds dual nationality, or presents inconsistencies or adverse records in passport data and background checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP-status disclosure and clearance report prepared by an approved compliance consultancy; comprehensive source-of-wealth file including asset registries, bank statements, employment certificates, and notarized affidavits; criminal record certificate; certified passport copies with translation; and a completed enhanced due diligence questionnaire processed by the bank's EDD unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Obscure corporate chain above the LLC with intermediate holdings in secrecy jurisdictions, generating UBO-opacity flags during correspondent-bank review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transparency package containing the full group organizational chart; each shareholder vehicle's register extract and UBO list; apostilled resolutions and powers of attorney; an accountant's report on economic substance of intermediate vehicles; a written commitment to disclose any 10% change in ownership within 15 days; and CRS self-certification forms for each account signatory.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital is injected via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank to the correspondent / Nostro account of the Egyptian collecting bank, with the payment order carrying the LLC's commercial-register number, tax identification number, and the CBE purpose classification for direct investment / equity subscription. The funds are credited to a segregated capital entry account and the bank issues a certificate of inward remittance, which the LLC files with GAFI to register the foreign-investment percentage; this certificate is the valuation benchmark for all future dividend, repatriation, and liquidation remittances. The MT103 must not reference loans, collateral, or personal purposes — loans above the CBE threshold require separate CBE external-financing registration and trigger thin-capitalization limitations. The beneficiary account name must match the LLC's incorporation file exactly to avoid rejection. After credit, the LLC may retain USD or convert to EGP at the interbank market rate; the bank's foreign-currency certificate must be permanently retained to substantiate exit remittances.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All outbound trade payments are cleared through the ACI/Nafeza import-control platform: the LLC must obtain a registered customs-order number for each shipment before the bank will execute any transfer or LC. Principal rails for the ISIC 2819 program are: (1) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for spare parts and advance payments within bank limits, marked with the capital-machinery import purpose code and payable only to registered suppliers; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit issued under UCP 600 in USD, EUR, or CNY in favor of the Chinese or EU component supplier, at sight or with usance up to 360 days, typically margin-funded at 15 to 25 percent, and incorporating transport documents, packing lists, and inspection certificates; (3) Documentary collections (D/P or D/A) for standardized low-value components where LC charges are uneconomic. For Chinese suppliers, the bank's USD/CNY dual-clearing corridor and CIPS-vs-SWIFT fee comparison should be evaluated. Each outbound payment must be reconciled within a 5 percent variance against the customs declaration; larger variances create arrears and suspension of trade-finance availability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP foreign-exchange forwards executed by licensed Egyptian banks under the CBE Foreign Exchange Regulations, permitted only against demonstrated underlying import, export, or registered investment exposure; typical tenors are 1 to 360 days with a 10 to 20 percent collateral margin and documentary triggers including LC drafts, purchase orders, and export contracts.

OTC cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) for balance-sheet hedging of the equity bridge and capex financing, subject to CBE notional reporting and an economic-substance test tied to the underlying bank facility.

Vanilla FX options (calls and puts) offered by tier-1 banks such as CIB, HSBC Egypt, and NBE to cap the USD cost of the import pipeline; premiums are cash-settled in EGP and exotic or leveraged structures are prohibited for non-financial corporate clients.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards in EGP are prohibited for Egyptian resident corporates: the CBE does not recognize offshore NDFs as a permissible hedging instrument for residents. The eligible substitute is a combination of onshore deliverable forwards and an FX collar with the relationship bank, priced against the CBE interbank fixing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the tax year; for calendar-year taxpayers on or before 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EGP 10,000–50,000 under Law 153/2020; delay tax at 2% per month on outstanding tax; compelled assessment; criminal enforcement in aggravated cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Approval and GAFI Deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Assembly of Shareholders and General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); Commercial Registry upon registration obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General Assembly convened within three months after fiscal year-end; financial statements deposited with GAFI within 30 days of approval (calendar-year companies by 31 May)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance warning from GAFI; late filing penalty of EGP 500 per month; administrative strike-off after repeated default or failure to respond to notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Application for renewal within three months before or after the fifth anniversary of initial registration; thereafter every five years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge of EGP 1,000; suspension of legal merchant status; administrative deregistration/strike-off after six months continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation at the Ordinary General Assembly; UBO register updated within 15 days of any shareholding or beneficial ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EGP 200,000 for inaccurate or non-maintained UBO data; director liability in cases of willful misdeclaration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All LLCs under Law 72/2017 must appoint one or more independent auditors; no revenue, capital, or shareholder threshold exempts the entity from a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) adopted as the national IFRS framework for standalone financial statements; IFRS as issued by the IASB for consolidated group reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The register of ultimate beneficial owners is a continual statutory record that must be updated within 15 days of any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership. At the annual General Assembly, managers confirm the completeness and accuracy of the register; auditors validate the UBO disclosure; the register is furnished to the AMLU or GAFI upon lawful demand.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% for Egyptian-resident limited liability companies under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005; a non-resident company's Egyptian permanent establishment is subject to the same 22.5% rate on Egypt-source profits; extractive petroleum/mining activities are taxed separately at 40.55% where specifically applicable.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday under the general regime. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 permits a deduction of up to 50% of eligible investment cost from taxable profits for qualifying trade and industrial projects in target governorates or strategic zones. A licensed free-zone company in a special economic zone such as the Suez Canal Economic Zone may obtain a full exemption from corporate income tax and VAT on qualifying export-oriented manufacturing activities for up to 15 years, subject to physical substance and GAFI licensing conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority's electronic filing portal; audited financial statements, tax reconciliation schedules, and the transfer pricing disclosure form must be attached.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Larger taxpayers may also be required to submit quarterly estimated corporate income tax payments, but the compliance return itself is filed once per tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year Egyptian LLC, the statutory filing and payment deadline is 30 April of the following year; if an approved different fiscal year-end applies, the deadline is the last day of the fourth month after that fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer legal identity: legal form, commercial registration number, Egyptian tax card number, head office address, and registered shareholding details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Egyptian LLC or permanent establishment address and Egyptian tax identification number. A foreign shareholder's address and foreign tax residency information must be disclosed, and a valid tax residence certificate should be uploaded when treaty relief is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period and basis of accounting: beginning and end dates of the tax year and the accounting standard used (Egyptian Accounting Standards or permitted IFRS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian PE or LLC fiscal period must match its own books; losses or profits of the foreign head office must never be consolidated into the Egyptian return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: total sales of high-power fiber laser metal sheet cutting systems, spare parts, engineering services, and related maintenance contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue economically attributable to the Egyptian LLC or PE, not only amounts invoiced by the Egyptian entity. The ETA may reattribute sales based on economic substance and substance-over-form principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales: direct materials, import duties, freight, factory overhead, direct labor, and inventory adjustment for the laser cutting machines and spare parts sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are restricted to expenses actually incurred by the Egyptian entity. Transfer prices on imported components or finished machines supplied by related foreign parties must be arm's length and documented under the local file rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: salaries and social insurance, rent, utilities, factory maintenance, travel, marketing, warranty costs, depreciation, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deductible expenses with Egyptian supporting documents are accepted. Management fees and head-office allocations paid to foreign shareholders are disallowed unless the Egyptian entity can prove actual services, commercial substance, and arm's length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory add-backs: non-deductible expenditure such as fines, bribes, excess entertainment, income tax itself, clients' withholding tax borne by the company, and artificial depreciation or provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE must add back all head-office administrative or royalty charges unless an applicable double tax treaty expressly permits their allocation; treaty-dependent PE profit attribution rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of prior-year tax losses: losses carried forward from prior Egyptian tax years, subject to the statutory five-year limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses realized by the Egyptian LLC or PE may be deducted. Foreign losses of the foreign parent or sister companies cannot be offset against Egyptian taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation and tax payable: application of the 22.5% rate, deduction of prepaid tax and withholding credits, and calculation of residual corporate income tax due with the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Unpaid tax must be remitted through the ETA electronic portal before the statutory deadline; a foreign shareholder's separate dividend withholding tax liability is not a credit against the LLC's own corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is punished by a fixed administrative fine generally between EGP 500 and EGP 5,000 per return. Unpaid tax accrues an additional monthly surcharge of 2% on the outstanding amount, calculated on calendar-day fractions, subject to a statutory cap generally not exceeding 50% of the tax due. Deliberate concealment or false returns escalate to criminal tax evasion penalties: imprisonment of two to five years, a fine equal to the tax evaded, and an additional discretionary fine in the range of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000. The ETA may also freeze bank accounts, suspend trade facilities, and prevent clearance of export shipments until the assessed tax and surcharges are settled.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax is imposed under Law No. 91 of 2005 on dividend and profit distributions made by an Egyptian limited liability company to its shareholders, whether resident or non-resident, except distributions made out of profits already exempted or subject to the preferential free-zone regime. Liguidation distributions attributable to accumulated profits in excess of paid-up capital may be taxed as deemed dividends at the same 10% rate; capital gains arising on liquidation are taxed separately at 22.5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double tax treaty, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain an original certificate of tax residence from the competent tax authority of the treaty country, have it legalized or apostilled and, if required, translated into Arabic, and submit an ETA withholding-tax relief application before the dividend distribution date. The application must state the treaty article, the percentage of ownership, and the beneficial ownership position. The ETA International Tax Department reviews the application and issues an approval instructing the Egyptian payer to apply the reduced treaty withholding rate. If merger relief is not obtained before payment, over-withheld tax may be recovered only through the ETA refund and assessment procedure using the same treaty documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory Egyptian withholding rate on cross-border royalties and debt interest paid to non-residents is 20%, unless the debtor is a bank or financial institution paying interest subject to a special statutory treatment. Under most Egyptian double tax treaties, royalties and interest are reduced to between 0% and 15%, commonly 10% for royalties and 10% for interest, provided the beneficial owner holds a valid tax residence certificate and no permanent establishment in Egypt gives rise to the income. Related-party interest payments are further subject to thin capitalization and arm's length scrutiny; excessive interest may be recharacterized as a hidden dividend distribution taxable at 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File preparation is triggered where a taxpayer's annual controlled transactions with related parties exceed EGP 20,000,000; the Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds EGP 500,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting is required where the group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds EGP 5,000,000,000. A TP disclosure schedule must accompany the corporate income tax return even when no full Local File is required. The ETA may request contemporaneous documentation below these thresholds in a risk-based audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has no precisely parallel Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the ETA vigorously applies substance-over-form, general anti-avoidance, and place-of-effective-management tests. A fiber-laser cutting machine manufacturer claiming Egyptian CIT benefits, free-zone tax exemption, treaty relief, or an Egyptian permanent establishment allocation must maintain real premises, production equipment, qualified engineers, independent board decisions, employment records, and active operational bank accounts in Egypt. A Spanish mailbox LLC with nominal staff and no local laser-equipment integration will be disregarded or recharacterized, with all related foreign sales reattributed to the Egyptian entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting export sales of fiber laser cutting machines, issuing forged commercial invoices, maintaining dual accounting books, or claiming fictitious deductions for phantom royalty payments to an offshore related company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for two to five years plus a fine equal to the tax evaded, a discretionary fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000, confiscation of goods and bank balances linked to the evasion, and civil assessment of the full tax deficiency with the 2% monthly late-payment surcharge up to 50%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers who sign or cause false returns to be filed are jointly and severally liable for the tax, surcharges, and fines. The ETA may impose travel bans, freeze personal assets, and pursue criminal imprisonment against responsible officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling finished fiber laser machines to a related foreign distributor at a 2% gross margin while the Egyptian LLC bears all manufacturing, warranty, and market risk; failing to prepare a Local File or to identify the most appropriate transfer pricing method; using long-term contracts materially below arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA makes a primary adjustment to the arm's length profit, denies deduction of the underpriced cost or overstated intercompany payment, assesses the resulting 22.5% corporate income tax with 2% monthly surcharge and, in cases of false documentation, refers the conduct to criminal prosecution for tax evasion with fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved intercompany pricing without economic justification are personally liable for the additional tax if they were aware or should have been aware of the artificial pricing; travel bans and seizure of personal assets are possible when the company fails to pay.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Qualifying for a Suez Canal Economic Zone free-zone license while the LLC has no Egyptian factory, no procurement staff, no assembly operations, and no technical engineers; the entity exists only to route machine sales through a related Cyprus or British Virgin Islands intermediary to avoid Egyptian tax and customs duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAFI and ETA jointly revoke the free-zone license, re-import duties are demanded, and accumulated undisclosed profits are taxed at 22.5% with penalties; the LLC may be struck off under the Egyptian Companies Law after investigations into false declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the shell is used as a façade, directors and shareholders can be pierced through the corporate veil and held personally liable for the company's unpaid tax duties and customs; personal travel bans, immigration alerts, and criminal sanctions apply for fraudulent free-zone licensing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring cash deposits into multiple accounts to avoid Financial Intelligence Unit reporting thresholds, executing wire transfers using shell intermediaries to sanctioned jurisdictions, or concealing the true beneficial owner through nominee shareholding in the Egyptian LLC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law No. 80 of 2002 and its executive regulations impose fines ranging from EGP 100,000 to EGP 500,000, imprisonment for five to fifteen years, confiscation of the laundered funds, and freezing of all related bank accounts and trade permits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML obligations are imposed on directors and compliance officers; a willfully blind director may be convicted of money laundering, barred from leave, placed on the CBE blacklist, and all personal assets connected to the transaction may be confiscated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits or royalties to a foreign shareholder without applying the statutory 10% dividend withholding tax or the 20% royalty/interest withholding tax; disguising such payments as 'cost reimbursement' without a service agreement, invoice, or withholding certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA holds the Egyptian LLC liable as the withholding and paying agent for the full withholding tax amount, plus 2% monthly late surcharge and non-deductible fines; deliberately mischaracterizing payments as nontaxable gives rise to criminal tax evasion liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director and any responsible board member are personally liable for the withheld but unremitted amounts; where the company is illiquid, the ETA may enforce directly against directors' assets and impose travel bans pending criminal proceeding.
